name: Thal'vireth
title: Thal'vireth, the Grove That Remembers
intro: The western realm, wrapped round the Verdant Tower. Six districts ring the Tower, each keeping its own pace of time; the White Road runs east from it to Nabireth, the only harbour. Beyond the forest lie the Sound and the Hushwood, the Elderwood west of them under the Antlers, and south across the Gulf the Desertborn's Sunward Reach. Choose any place for what the Compendium says of it.

special.Ix'kaanil: The Tower, and seat of the High Priestess

lore.text: The realm’s only legal harbour, built on piers over the shallows at the head of the Quiet Gulf, and its largest town by the outside count, at about eighteen thousand.
The Balam port on the Gulf's western arm, and the fjord-folk's landlord.

The Verdant Tower and the tree grown through it, with the Canopy Court in its lower boughs and the Sanctum Root beneath. Seat of the High Priestess, and the realm's capital in every sense but the one a census would recognise: about fourteen thousand live in its boughs and at its roots.

A town of inns a few days below the Canopy Steps, where the Root-Road crosses the White Road. Its re-acclimation houses sell rest at true time and are the accepted cure for Count-sickness; its ground-floor rooms receive the slow procession on its way to the Waiting Wards.

A town of about seven thousand at the Road’s midpoint, built around the square of the Exchange Houses, where foreign coin is changed for jade-tally and chronoflow contracts are written and sealed. The cartel benches, the contract-rooms and Arnabar Cinnatrage’s table are all here, and so are most of the Road’s lawyers.
The great terraced hillside north of the White Road, and the Cradle's largest town. About six lived years to one outside year.
Where the harvest is weighed and stamped, and where the Granary Road begins.
An orchard village on the Granary Road, famous for the honey of stingless forest bees.
The Wards' heart, with the Wall and the oldest Iteration Houses. About four lived years to one outside year.
The furnace-halls under the cloudglass lattice; the only place in the realm where soulstone is worked.
The realm's archive, grown out of the living root north of the Tower. A month per outside year at the outer stacks, a few days in the inner.
Named for the wayeb, the nameless days at the end of the old calendar when nothing is begun. The dying are kept here at a day or so per outside year.
The wardens' camp at the head of the only sanctioned way down. Its pace below is not published.

north, east, south and west, named for the four quarters in the old tongue. Xamanir faces the Witzaran ice; Lak'inir the Gulf shore north of Nabireth; Noholir the Gulf Islands; Chik'inir the head of the Long Trail.

The Desertborn caravan-market on the Long Trail, and the nearest thing the Reach has to a town.
A trading camp on the Flame road near the Iron Hordes frontier.
Deep wells in the red desert, held by whichever clan held them last.
A camp in the far south, named for the one cloud a year it is said to get.
The largest fishing village on the Sound.
A sealing hamlet at the Sound's northern mouth.
Balam outposts in the northern pines; Witzir faces the Obsidian Crown.

A village south of the Road where the Granary Road and three Strands meet, and the last place on the way to the sea where a carter can change oxen. Its name is a joke at the expense of everyone who arrives in it on foot after the oxen have all been hired.

Two villages of the Landing a day’s walk out: Najeleth, the house-road, at the head of a Strand north of the Road, where Nabireth’s carters and porters keep their families; and Ki’eleth, the sweet road, a hamlet on the Granary Road south of it, where the Cradle’s fruit and honey wait in cool sheds for a ship.

A village on the shore just south of Nabireth, beside the stream that gives the harbour its fresh water. Its people fill and sell ships’ water by the barrel, ferry passengers out to vessels at anchor during the wayeb, and keep the only boat-yard in the realm that will repair a foreign hull.

A village on the stone itself at the second Stone, with a market-square on either side of the Road, where Strands from both halves of the Cradle come in. On market mornings Kaajeleth’s strand-gates are the busiest in the realm.

A hamlet on a stream a day and a half short of the Canopy Steps, where foreigners waiting on the Court lodge when the Steps are too crowded to sleep on. Its houses are let by the week and its one shrine is kept, by long custom, for gods the realm does not have.

A village on the stone at the sixth Stone, below Weneleth, where the Strands begin to leave the Road in earnest. Its strand-gate is the oldest on the Road, and the village is named for it.
Balamir. The name means 'dance-watch, a lodge'.
The Sound. The name means 'black water'.
The Sound. The name means 'white water'.
The realm’s only post on the Elderwood’s edge, a day’s walk west of the Long Trail where it comes down to Ek’thalas, at the south-eastern foot of the Antlers.
